asks: Calgary Board of Education trustees support the added Calgary seats and ask the commission to avoid hybrid ridings (Calgary-Cross, Calgary-West-Elbow, Calgary-Okotoks) and keep municipal integrity.
Asks that Blackfalds be placed in the new Innisfail riding rather than a Lacombe-Ponoka riding.
Asks the commission not to divide Beaumont between ridings.
Asks the commission to reconsider dividing Beaumont.
Asks that Weinlos, Crawford Plains and Laurel north of Anthony Henday be placed in Edmonton-Meadows.
Supports the interim proposal for St. Albert as keeping the city together as far as possible.

quote: I support the commissions current proposal as it supports the cohesion of the community of St. Albert as much as possible
note: Header: St. Albert resident writing about proposed 82 - St. Albert. Supports the interim arrangement (S0 pattern). Adds that making St. Albert into two ridings eventually makes more sense than aligning parts with rural edges, a lean toward S3 as a future state, not asked for now.

asks: Supports the interim report, keeping districts either inside or outside city boundaries, and the Edmonton-Strathcona riding as drawn.
Asks for an Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills riding bounded by Highway 22 on the west and the Red Deer River on the east, including Irricana and Beiseker, instead of the interim Mountain View-Kneehill.

quote: Keeping the western boundary at Highway 22 ensures that the riding remains focused on communities with similar rural and agricultural interests rather than incorporating areas with vastly different geographic and economic profiles.
note: Olds resident; header about 75 - Mountain View-Kneehill. Proposed boundaries: west Highway 22, east Red Deer River, south 'Include the communities of Irricana and Beiseker' (p. 12). Crossfield is not named. Says the interim Mountain View-Kneehill 'will result in less effective representation', short of arguing against O2 by its terms. Does not name Rocky Mountain House or Sundre.

asks: Asks that Beaumont be kept whole within Leduc-Beaumont.
Asks that Edmonton not lose a seat and that one be added instead.
Asks that Red Deer-North keep its 2023 boundaries, without the rural areas the writer sees added to the north.

quote: We would like to see the boundaries for Red Deer North stay the same as last provincial election 2023.
note: Writer believes the interim Red Deer-North added rural areas to the north and objects: 'issues effecting urban areas and rural areas maybe be different. This makes it difficult for an elected representative to be fair to both areas.' Wants the city riding kept as in 2023 (wholly in the city). The objection to rural additions cuts against R2 in kind but the four-way plan is not described, so rejects left blank.

asks: Asks that Beaumont not be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks the commission not to take a seat from Edmonton.
Says no changes to electoral boundaries are wanted or required.
Asks that half of Beaumont not be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park (add Tofield instead) and that Heritage Hills not be carved out.
Asks that Heritage Hills stay in Sherwood Park.
Asks that Beaumont and Leduc areas not be joined to Strathcona-Sherwood Park; suggests adding Tofield instead.
MLA asks that the interim Fort Saskatchewan-Vegreville boundary stay unchanged, keeping the Strathcona County area north of Highway 16 in it.
Asks that Beaumont not be made part of Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks the commission to abandon the Calgary-Okotoks hybrid and keep Calgary-Shaw an urban riding inside city limits.
Asks that the Looma area of Leduc County remain in the Maskwacis-Wetaskiwin constituency.
Asks that Beaumont not be divided and stay in Leduc-Beaumont.
Asks that the Fort Saskatchewan-Vegreville boundaries remain as they are.
Asks that Heritage Hills not be removed and Beaumont/Leduc not be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks that Heritage Hills stay in Strathcona-Sherwood Park and Beaumont not be added.

Calgary Ward 13 councillor asks the commission to reject both interim options for south Calgary, especially Calgary-Okotoks, and to reflect south Calgary growth without joining city communities to separate municipalities.
Fort Macleod resident with a business in Lethbridge asks that any boundary changes be made so as to bridge the gap between urban and rural interests.

note: Fort Macleod resident (Livingstone-Macleod) who operates a business in Lethbridge asks that boundary changes 'bridge the gap between urban and rural interests and concerns' and says 'If our electoral boundaries are moved, there will be more ability to reach out and unify our communities'. Lethbridge is named only as where his business is; no arrangement for the city is stated. Could be read as L2 direction; narrower code chosen (rule 17).

asks: Edmonton councillor thanks the commission for keeping Edmonton ridings inside the city, asks for a riding to be added for growth, and objects to removing Edmonton-Riverview.

note: St. Albert named in passing: residents of 'Sherwood Park and St. Albert' would likely appreciate boundaries that fit their communities. No request (rule 6).

asks: Asks that Heritage Hills stay in Strathcona-Sherwood Park and Beaumont/Leduc not be added.
Asks the commission to preserve Edmonton-Riverview as its own electoral division.
Asks that Lethbridge be divided into quarters, each joined with surrounding rural area, to give the city a larger voice.

quote: a possible way to do that would be to divide Lethbridge into quarters & include rural ridings in each quarter
note: Lethbridge resident; header about 70 - Lethbridge-West, issue ticked 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. Describes the four-quarter city-and-country design. Offered as 'a possible way'.

asks: Supports the interim Calgary-Glenmore riding and asks for no further changes to it.
Supports the interim proposal for Edmonton-South West and asks for an added seat in Edmonton.
Thanks the commission for not creating hybrid ridings and warns that adding Riverview to Edmonton-Glenora makes too large a population.
Asks that Conrich be moved out of the rural Chestermere-Strathmore riding into a Calgary riding.

note: Form header names 57 - Chestermere-Strathmore as the district, but the message is only about Conrich, which the Calgary writer wants moved into a Calgary riding. Says nothing of the City of Chestermere.

asks: Asks that Beaumont not be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park, that Heritage Hills stay, and that Tofield be added if population is needed.
Town of Coaldale asks to remain in its current electoral district (Taber-Warner), aligned with the Highway 3 corridor.

note: Town of Coaldale asks only to 'remain within its current provincial electoral district' (Taber-Warner). The letter describes Coaldale's community of interest as the Highway 3 corridor 'anchored by Lethbridge' and embedded with 'Lethbridge, Taber, and the surrounding rural municipalities', but never says Coaldale should or should not share a district with part of the city (rule 8). Several passages match EBC-2025-2-0537's corridor argument nearly word for word.

asks: Town of Rocky Mountain House asks that the town and all of Clearwater County be kept in one constituency connected with other Eastern Slopes communities, not joined with Lacombe.

quote: Rocky Mountain will have the best representation by being located in the same constituency as all of Clearwater County and maintaining a connection with other communities along the Eastern Slopes region.
note: Town of Rocky Mountain House, mayor and council. Rejects the interim division (p. 85: 'we urge the Commission to keep Rocky Mountain House and Clearwater County together within a single constituency'). Also argues against pairing with Lacombe (p. 84: 'including Rocky Mountain House with Lacombe County, the City of Lacombe, and other proposed eastern communities within the Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House boundary risks reducing representation'; p. 85: 'Rocky Mountain House has always faced west, not east'), hence W2 in rejects. Sundre is named only through the Rocky Mountain House-Sundre-Cochrane tourism zone. No mention of Banff park.

asks: Asks the commission to adopt the four-quadrant hybrid model for Lethbridge and its surrounding rural municipalities.

quote: I write to urge the Commission to adopt the four-quadrant hybrid model for Lethbridge and its surrounding rural municipalities.
note: Lethbridge resident, seven pages. Reacts to the interim report's decision not to adopt the hybrid model. Rejection of L1 on p. 91: 'The hybrid model better reflects actual regional relationships than the current two-division configuration, which rests largely on historical convenience rather than present-day regional function.' Corridor passages recur in EBC-2025-2-0535 and EBC-2025-2-0552.

asks: Penhold councillor asks that Innisfail-Sylvan Lake be shaped as a QEII corridor riding, adding Blackfalds and Trochu.

note: Penhold councillor wants Innisfail-Sylvan Lake aligned 'with the natural corridor of the Queen Elizabeth II (QEII) Highway and the regional centre of Red Deer', adding Blackfalds and Trochu. Red Deer is named as the hub the towns look to; the letter does not say any town should share a district with part of the city (codebook note under REDDEER). Attached map (p. 96) is unreadable in OCR.

asks: Asks that Calgary south-east be made two ridings without splitting Cranston, and that urban and rural ridings stay separate.
Asks that Sherwood Park and Strathcona County ridings be left as they are, without the added communities.
Supports the interim map keeping Calgary-Foothills inside the City of Calgary with no rural areas.
Town of Coalhurst asks to keep its current electoral boundary and opposes the westward extension of Livingstone-Macleod to Pincher Creek and Crowsnest Pass.
Asks that Jasper stay in West Yellowhead rather than be joined with Banff.
Opposes adding Beaumont to the Sherwood Park area riding and dropping Heritage Hills.

Foothills School Division asks the commission to weigh the combined effect of the interim changes on its communities (Okotoks options, Banff-Jasper, Cochrane-Springbank, High River-Vulcan), preferring Okotoks with Diamond Valley over Calgary-Okotoks; the chair's attached personal form asks that Priddis-area Foothills not be put in Banff-Jasper.

note: Foothills School Division lists 'the movement of northern Foothills areas into Cochrane–Springbank' among interim changes affecting it. District named; no request about who Cochrane shares a district with.

asks: Supports the interim Edmonton-Castle Downs with no hybrid, and objects to the loss of an inner-city Edmonton riding.
Asks that Beaumont not be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks that Jasper not be combined with Banff and stay tied to Hinton and the east.
Inglewood Community League president objects that the merged Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview would be over-populated and asks how that is equitable.

Mountain View County council asks that residents west of Highway 22 be placed in a western-facing constituency, keeping the current boundary between Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre and Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills.

quote: Placing residents living west of Highway 22 in a prairie riding like Mountain View-Kneehill would limit their effective representation in the Alberta Legislature.
note: Mountain View County council. Asks to keep the current Highway 22 line between the foothills riding and Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills (p. 127), which leaves Sundre and western Mountain View County out of the prairie riding. Speaks only to the western boundary; Crossfield, Irricana and Beiseker are not mentioned.

quote: Our recommendation would be to maintain the same boundary through Mountain View County that currently exists between Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre and Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills.
note: Wants residents west of Highway 22 'included in a western-facing constituency' and cites their ties with 'Sundre, Rocky Mountain House, and Clearwater County' (p. 126). Does not ask in terms to keep the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding or say anything about Clearwater County's own treatment, hence direction.

asks: Supports the interim map keeping Calgary and Edmonton ridings inside city limits and asks for one more Calgary riding.
Coaldale resident asks the commission to adopt the four-quadrant hybrid model for Lethbridge and the surrounding region.

quote: The four quadrant hybrid meets each criterion more precisely than the status quo.
note: Coaldale resident (name matches a Coaldale councillor copied on EBC-2025-2-0535); header about 85 - Taber-Warner. Names the four-quadrant hybrid binding 'Lethbridge, Coaldale, Taber, the MD of Taber, and Lethbridge County to Lethbridge's hub'. Prefers it to the status quo; no separate words of rejection. Shares argument and phrasing with EBC-2025-2-0537.

asks: Cypress County rancher asks that Cypress County not be merged into a blended riding with Medicine Hat, so it has rural representation.
Asks that Jasper be kept in West Yellowhead rather than placed in Banff-Jasper.
Asks that Nordegg, Rocky Mountain House and all of Clearwater County be kept in one constituency, with western Clearwater County taken out of Banff-Jasper.

quote: keep Nordegg, Rocky Mountain House, and all of Clearwater County within a single constituency
note: Clearwater County resident (Cline River), tourism operator; header: current 80 - Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre, about 53 - Banff-Jasper. Asks only that the county and town stay together; nothing about Sundre, Lacombe or what else is in the riding.

quote: I believe that the inclusion of western Clearwater County in a riding with Banff and Jasper National Park will reduce the effective representation of our region.
note: Rejects the interim Banff-Jasper taking western Clearwater County. Reasons given: no shared relationship with Parks Canada, Highway 93 closures, David Thompson tourism zone runs from Rocky Mountain House 'all the way to the border with Banff National Park'. The reasoning treats the parks as a separate region, which also cuts against joining park land to the Rocky riding, but B1 was not before him and he does not say where the parks should go, so no want and B1 not listed.

asks: Opposes moving Beaumont into Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks that boundaries reflect that Rimbey, Bentley and Benalto have more in common with Sylvan Lake and Lacombe.
